statements.title: 28 stesen seismik perkukuh pemantauan gempa di Sabah
statements.summary: Follows a weak M3.3 earthquake at Kuamut, Kinabatangan, at 5.32 am on 26 Sep 2026. MET Malaysia monitors Sabah 24 hours a day through 28 seismic stations, releases earthquake information within 6 minutes of detection (subject to data availability), and says earthquakes cannot be predicted in time, place or magnitude.

statements.title: Permulaan fasa peralihan monsun
statements.summary: The monsoon transition phase is expected to start on 9 Oct 2026 and last to the end of October, ending the Southwest Monsoon that began 14 May 2026. Thunderstorms with heavy rain, lightning and strong winds are possible, mostly in the afternoon and early evening in the west and interior of the Peninsula and west Sabah and Sarawak, with possible flash floods and fallen trees. Transboundary haze is expected to ease gradually as wind direction changes. Hotline 1-300-22-1638.

statements.title: Forum Iklim Kebangsaan 2026
statements.summary: The Northeast Monsoon 2026/2027 is expected to start at the end of October 2026 and last to mid-March 2027, usually bringing continuous heavy rain to the East Coast of the Peninsula, east Sabah and west Sarawak, with higher flood and landslide risk. El Nino is developing and expected to strengthen by the end of 2026. Extreme rain above 150 mm a day may still occur early in the monsoon: two to three events in East Coast states and one to two in southern Sarawak expected. From January 2027 drier, hotter conditions may raise heat-wave, drought and local haze risk if open burning or forest fires occur. myCuaca 3.0 app launched.

statements.title: Gempa bumi kuat di berhampiran Pantai Timur Kamchatka
statements.summary: M6.8 earthquake near the east coast of Kamchatka at 11:35 am on 16 Oct 2026, at 51.9 N 157.5 E, depth 125 km, 152 km south-west of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, Russia. No tsunami threat to Malaysia. Not an ASEAN event.
